gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Visitor has gaping-mouthed e's and stroke ends that look cut from one ribbon, pure pixel-era nostalgia. Noto Sans Armenian takes over with a plain sans, tall full s and z shapes, and round letters that stay inviting down a whole page.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Visitor brings a nostalgic, digital heading with no calligraphic shading to steer the eye, just flat, pulled-through strokes. And Noto Sans Avestan follows with a pronounced x-height and curves whose tips never quite touch, so the text feels modern and open.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Noto Sans Balinese keeps its curved glyphs breathing and its ascenders short, giving a modern, professional sans-serif texture to the text. Visitor is the loud one, with curves and straights sharing a single width.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Noto Sans Bamum reads clean and modern, its curved strokes stopping short of turning inward and every small letter wide open. And over a full page that plain sans keeps going easily, while Visitor's bent-tubing letters stay up top.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-bassa-va: Nostalgic is the first word for Visitor, whose strokes look drawn with one constant pen width, like solder through a nozzle. But Noto Sans Bassa Vah has a dominant midsection and an open-jawed c, so a long page of this sans feels contemporary and steady.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-batak: Visitor has a marker-drawn plainness in every character, with big bowls under short ascenders. And Noto Sans Batak, a plain sans with a towering x-height and an e that never looks squeezed shut, makes paragraphs feel approachable.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Noto Sans Bengali has capitals barely taller than its lowercase and distinctly open letter mouths. And a long page of this sans-serif reads contemporary and smooth, while Visitor's thin-looking letters with no thinner parts stay in the heading.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuk: Visitor's pen never changes pressure or angle, and its e's gape wide. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki is the one built for reading, with swollen lowercase and easy open apertures, while Visitor simply announces.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Noto Sans Brahmi has a high mean line and open-ended curves, set against Visitor's round letters drawn like bent wire. Noto Sans Brahmi is best given a comfortable size, so that sans can show its open curves.
gen-dafont-visitor-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Noto Sans Buginese leaves its letter mouths open like unjoined chalk arcs. Its short ascenders and modern sans shapes let a long page move along, while Visitor's uninterrupted line width stays in the heading.
